facts.text: Tláhuac began as a pre‑Hispanic city‑state founded by the Chichimecas in the 13th century before joining the Aztec Empire.
The borough’s main landmark is the San Francisco de Asís parish church, established in 1547 during the early colonial period.
The Museo Regional Tláhuac, opened in 2018, showcases local artifacts in a human‑scale setting that brings the area’s intimate history to life.
Tláhuac’s terrain was once part of the lakebeds where Lake Chalco and Lake Xochimilco met, and the town of San Pedro Tláhuac originally sat on an island.
An extinct volcano, Volcán de la Estrella, once supplied tezontle stone that helped build Mexico City’s historic center.
In 1924, residents of Tláhuac successfully petitioned for autonomy, separating the borough from Xochimilco and becoming its own municipality.
